description:
FILED s473t5f (#1501 round 7, uni/, 2026-09-13).  PRE-EXISTING; ASCII-probed,
so it is NOT the #418 non-ASCII-label family the round's brief guessed.

A `goto LABEL` whose target label sits in a NESTED BLOCK emits a `(go :LABEL)`
at the OUTER tagbody, where no such tag exists.  That is a COMPILE-time CL
error, so the whole top-level form is lost:

    {
        no warnings;
        goto HERE;
        if (undef) {
            HERE: { print "goto ASCII LABEL works\n"; }
        }
    }
    print "done\n";

    perl: "goto ASCII LABEL works" then "done"
    PCL : "attempt to GO to nonexistent tag: :HERE" -- the block's whole form
          is abandoned; only "done" prints.

The emission shows it exactly: the outer `(tagbody :redo (go :HERE) (p-if
(p-undef) (progn â¦ (block HERE â¦))) :next)` -- the labelled block is lowered
as a CL `block`/`catch` nest inside the `p-if`, and there is no `:HERE`
tagbody tag anywhere.

perl's rule: `goto LABEL` may not jump INTO a construct that requires
initialization (a sub, a `foreach`), but a plain nested BLOCK is a legal
target, and perl finds the label dynamically.

THIS IS #1654's WARNED-ABOUT FAILURE MODE, from the other side.  #1654 ("t/op/
goto.t's SECOND blocker") says of the standalone-label branch: "a narrower
[scan] emits a `(go â¦)` with no reachable tag, which is a load-time CL error,
not a perl-shaped one".  That is precisely what this shape already does --
so the two are one piece of work: the forward/nested `goto` needs a real
mechanism (a dynamic catch/throw keyed by label, the way `last LABEL` already
works), not another textual gate.

RULE 12 BOUNDARY: a jump is EFFECT-ONLY, so until the mechanism exists the
compiler should ANNOUNCE on stderr and emit a run-time perl-shaped die at the
goto, instead of an unreachable `(go â¦)` that kills the form at LOAD time.
That interim is worth doing on its own: it converts "the rest of the block
vanishes" into "one statement dies loudly", and it is what makes the cost of
the real fix measurable.

WHAT IT COSTS: `t/uni/labels.t` row 10 (its `goto UTF-8 LABEL works.`) plus
the 2 rows the file never reaches.  t/op/goto.t's 134 rows sit behind #1654.

DO NOT RETRY: reading the label's block as a sibling and hoisting the tag out
of the `p-if` -- the tag would then be reachable but the BLOCK's own
`last`/`next`/`redo` catches and its lexical scope would move with it.


=== DONE (s517a, member 0, commit 444767ff, 2026-10-15) ===
The mechanism the task asked for, built: a goto into a nested block is a
dynamic catch/throw keyed by label plus an ENTRY FLAG that steers the path.
Parser2 `_classify_nested_gotos` (pre-pass after _rewrite_unreachable_gotos)
finds, for every literal `goto L`, the lowest block holding both the goto and
L; when L's statement is not a direct child of it, the path is recorded
(if-clause blocks, path statements with earlier siblings).  `_goto_nested_fire`
(top of _lower_block_1, the common list) binds F and lowers forward gotos via
`(setf F (catch T PREFIX nil))` and gotos inside/after the label's statement
via the new runtime macro `p-goto-region` (re-runs on `(throw T 1)`); the
if-chain on the path gets `(p-if F 1 TEST)` / earlier `(p-if F nil TEST)`,
earlier siblings `(p-if F nil (progn ...))`, and F clears at the label.  The
"DO NOT RETRY" hoist was NOT used: the label's block keeps its own
last/next/redo catches and lexical scope; the common list's lexicals keep
their values (guard row).
DIES at the goto instead of a CL compile error: foreach target (perl text
`Can't "goto" into the middle of a foreach loop`); while/until/C-for body,
do/eval/map block, a declaration on the way -> `PCL: unsupported goto into
...` (residue #3320).
Numbers: reproducer = perl; Text-CSV 15_flags.t 8/1 (ran 9 of 229) -> 223/6,
the 6 = #1389 (real perl fails the same six with *utf8::is_utf8 = sub {1}).
Guard Pl/t/goto-label-01.t 13 -> 20, the 7 new rows all FAIL on dc87c403.
corpus-diff vs dc87c403: 1 of 111 (eval.t: its foreach-goto row now dies with
perl's text where it was a (go :foo) compile error); drops 5 unchanged.
uni/labels.t row 10 (the original report) is a companion-file check.
subject: goto LABEL whose target is in a NESTED BLOCK emits an unreachable (go :LABEL) -- a compile-time CL error that loses the whole top-level form; #1654 warned about exactly this shape (ASCII-probed)
